paragraphs: Hi Emma, my name is Valentina Ríos, but my nickname is Vale. I am your new pen friend from the English club. I am nineteen years old and I am a student at a university in Cali, Colombia.

2.title: A Day in the Life of a Coffee Farmer
paragraphs: Don Ernesto is a coffee farmer in Salento, Quindío. His day starts very early. He always wakes up at four thirty, and he gets up at five. He drinks a cup of black coffee and eats breakfast with his wife: arepas, eggs and cheese.
At six o'clock he goes to the farm. He usually works with two young men from the town. They pick the red coffee cherries by hand. It takes about four hours to fill ten big baskets.
Lunch is at twelve. After lunch, Don Ernesto sleeps for thirty minutes. In the afternoon he dries the coffee beans in the sun.

He finishes work at five and takes a bus to the town square. He talks with his friends there. Dinner is at seven, and he goes to bed at nine. On weekends he doesn't work. He watches football on Sunday afternoons.
What time does he wake up on weekends? Late — at six!

2.title: Questions for a Night Nurse

What time do you start work? I start at seven in the evening and I finish at seven in the morning.
When do you sleep? I sleep in the day, from nine in the morning to three in the afternoon. My room is very dark and quiet.
What do you eat at night? I usually take lunch from home — rice, chicken and salad. At two in the morning I eat a sandwich with my colleagues.

What do you do on your free days? On weekdays I work, but on weekends I see my family. We have dinner together on Saturdays.
Is it difficult? Sometimes, yes. But I love my job. People need nurses every hour of every day.

3.title: Which Phone Is Better?
paragraphs: I want a new phone, so this week I compare two models: the Nova 5 and the Lumo X. Here is my review.

This phone, the Nova 5, costs 600,000 pesos. It is light and the screen is big. The camera is good, but the battery is not great. That phone, the Lumo X, costs 900,000 pesos. It is heavier than the Nova, but the battery is better — two days with one charge!
Which one is more comfortable? The Nova is thinner, so it is more comfortable in my hand. Which one is more beautiful? I like the colours of the Lumo: blue, green and gold.

Is the Lumo X worth 300,000 pesos more? For me, no. I use my phone for photos and messages, and the Nova is cheaper. My final choice is the Nova 5. It is not perfect, but it is a good phone for a good price.

paragraphs: It is Friday evening. Jaime and his girlfriend, Natalia, meet at La Esquina, a small café in Medellín. A waiter comes to their table.
'Good evening. Would you like something to drink?' 'Yes, please,' says Natalia. 'Could I have a lemonade with coconut?' 'And I would like a coffee, please,' says Jaime.

At the end, Jaime wants to pay, but Natalia stops him. 'No, it's my turn. You paid last time.' Jaime laughs. 'OK, thank you. Next time I'll invite you.' The waiter brings two free cookies. 'Help yourselves!'

Where are the children? A lot of my cousins are playing in the garden. My little cousin Juanita is crying because she wants the ball. My mother is looking after her.

paragraphs: Our English class asked twenty students at Colegio San José about their free time. Here are the results of our survey.

7.title: My Weekend in Cartagena
paragraphs: Last weekend I travelled to Cartagena with my best friend, Laura. We had a great time!
We arrived on Friday night. The flight from Bogotá was short — only one hour and a half. We stayed in a small hotel in Getsemaní. It wasn't expensive, and the people were very friendly.

On Saturday morning we walked around the old city. The streets were beautiful and full of colour. Then we bought fruit from a palenquera — mango and watermelon. After that, we took a boat to the Rosario Islands. The water was blue and warm.
On Sunday, something funny happened. A parrot stole Laura's hat at the beach! We laughed a lot. The museum in the afternoon was a bit boring, but the dinner was delicious.
We came back the day before yesterday. Two days ago I was on the beach, and now I'm at the office. Life is hard!

7.title: The Lost Bag
paragraphs: Yesterday was a strange day for Andrés. He took a bus from Bucaramanga to Bogotá early in the morning. The trip was long — nine hours — and boring.
When the bus arrived at the terminal, Andrés got off and walked to a taxi. Then he stopped. Where was his bag? It wasn't with him! His laptop and his clothes were inside.

He ran back to the bus, but it wasn't there. Andrés was very worried. He went to the bus company office. A woman there called the driver. 'Yes,' she said after a few minutes, 'your bag is on the bus. The driver is coming back.'
Andrés waited for forty minutes. After that, the bus came back and the driver gave him the bag. Andrés said thank you and gave him a small present: a box of bocadillos from Santander.
Last night he told the story to his family. 'Never again,' he said.

paragraphs: La Candelaria is the old neighbourhood in the centre of Bogotá. It's small, so everything is within walking distance.

There are a lot of museums here. The Botero Museum is on Calle 11, across from a small library. There is a big square, Plaza de Bolívar, between the Cathedral and the Congress. It's very crowded on weekends.

Are there any good places to eat? Yes, there are! There is a famous café on the corner of Calle 10 and Carrera 2. They sell chocolate with cheese. There are a few small restaurants on the next block, too.
How much money do you need? Not a lot. Many museums are free on Sundays. How many days do you need? One or two days is enough.

11.title: Review: Hostal Las Palmas, Minca
paragraphs: Last month I stayed three nights at Hostal Las Palmas in Minca, a small village in the mountains near Santa Marta. Was it worth it? Yes!
The place is really beautiful. There are hammocks, birds and an extremely green garden. The rooms are quite small, though, and the showers are a bit cold. However, the beds are pretty comfortable.
The food is excellent because the owner, Doña Inés, cooks with fruit and vegetables from her farm. Breakfast is included, so you don't pay extra.

What should you do in Minca? You should visit the waterfalls in the morning, because they are quiet before ten. You can also take a coffee tour. I really recommend the tour with Don Hernán — it's cheap and very interesting.

First, you should read about the hotel. It's pretty easy: look at its website. You can learn a bit about its history and its guests.
Second, you should practise your answers with a friend. Interviewers usually ask 'Why do you want this job?', so prepare a good answer.
Third, you shouldn't arrive late. Bogotá traffic is quite bad, so leave home early. However, don't arrive too early, either — ten minutes before is perfect.
Finally, you can wear simple, clean clothes. You don't need a suit, though. Smile, because hotels love friendly people!

14.title: Colombia: A Country of Records
paragraphs: Colombia is a country of incredible nature. It has two coasts — the Caribbean and the Pacific — and three mountain ranges.

How high is the highest mountain? The Pico Cristóbal Colón is roughly 5,700 metres high. It's in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, only 42 kilometres from the sea. It's one of the highest coastal mountains in the world.
The longest river in Colombia is the Magdalena. How long is it? About 1,500 kilometres. The deepest lake is Lake Tota in Boyacá. It's roughly 60 metres deep.
Colombia also has very different climates. La Guajira has a dry desert, and the Chocó is one of the most humid places on Earth. It rains there almost every day!

What about cities? Bogotá is by far the largest city. Its population is about eight million people — roughly three times bigger than Medellín's. And the country is big: it's roughly twice as big as France. The Amazon rainforest covers about a third of it.

paragraphs: Ten years ago, I was a shy teenager in Montería. I used to hate speaking in front of people, and my English was terrible. Nowadays I'm twenty-five and I work in a call centre in Barranquilla. I speak English every day!
How did my life change? After school I decided to take a free English course online. I practised every night. Then I got this job. These days my English has improved a lot, but I want more.
